patch.value: Phase 4: pm-vcs versions its own source

The package must track its own source code in pm-vcs alongside git, so the claim that pm-vcs is a working version control system is demonstrated by the repository itself rather than asserted in a README. The self-hosted history ships as a bundle in the repository and a CI gate proves the bundle's tip tree is exactly the source tree, so source cannot change without the pm-vcs history following it.

A tracked bundle holds pm-vcs history of pm-vcs's own source; a CI gate fails when the bundle's tip tree differs from the git-tracked source in any byte; the gate re-verifies every object against its own id; the check is deterministic and cannot pass by regenerating the bundle from a dirty tree

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Design: a committed text bundle (selfhost.bundle) holds pm-vcs history of the git-tracked source. accept:self-host is verify-only: it reads the committed bundle and the committed source both from HEAD (git cat-file / git archive), so a dirty working tree cannot affect the verdict and regenerating the bundle without committing it changes nothing. self-host:write is the only path that writes the bundle. The exclusion set is data in self-host.json; the gate builds its source tree from git ls-files minus exclusions, so a tracked file in neither the bundle nor the exclusion set fails closed. Trees use the legacy (FileId-free) v1 encoding via engine buildTree so the bundle is deterministic — tree ids depend only on content+mode. parseBundle re-hashes every object against its own id (point 3); importBundleObjects stores them. Byte-exactness = root tree id equality, which covers content and mode.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Implemented scripts/self-host.ts with --write/--check separation, self-host.json data file, selfhost.bundle committed artifact, test/self-host.test.ts (15 real tests), wired accept:self-host into package.json release:check and CI, documented in ARCHITECTURE.md section 10. Verified coverage 100/100/100 with the locked pm-cli 2026.8.1 (a stale local node_modules at 2026.8.3 had silently changed the test harness and dropped the pmClient fallback branch from coverage; npm ci restored the locked version).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round on PR 10 addressed. Five reviewer findings fixed: git ls-files read NUL-delimited so a newline in a path cannot desynchronise the gate's own path list; readSourceFiles now raises the absent-path failure its docstring already promised, which also removed an unreachable missing-path diagnostic in main that could never fire; extractHead materializes HEAD through a detached git worktree instead of git archive piped to tar, removing the only non-git binary the gate depended on and which the Windows job never exercised despite accept:self-host sitting inside release:check and prepublishOnly; spawnSync launch failures are distinguished from non-zero exits so a missing git cannot read as a clean verdict; and loadConfig, non-commit ref tips and object omission all gained real tests. One finding was rejected as a false positive: Sourcery called import.meta.dirname non-standard, but it landed in Node 20.11 and this package declares engines node >=22.18.0 with a green 22 and 26 matrix. CodeRabbit accepted that rebuttal. A sixth defect surfaced from the review rather than in it: the gate did not prove the bundle is SELF-CONTAINED. verifySelfHost resolves the tip through a store the source side has already written every blob into, so a bundle omitting an object it declares still resolved by borrowing the missing bytes from the source, and parseBundle accepts a header listing an object the body omits — meaning a truncated bundle was reported byte-identical. The declared object list is now compared against the lines actually carried, the only check in the function that consults no store. Verified the whole loop end to end: committed the source, watched the gate fail exit 1 naming both changed files and both tree ids, regenerated the bundle, watched it pass.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Addressed the coverage round: added scripts/self-host.ts to coverageGate.sources, fixed the NODE_V8_COVERAGE lcov corruption by overriding it to /dev/null in test helpers, exported the script's private functions and main for testability, wrote 18 new tests bringing scripts/self-host.ts to a genuine 100/100/100 (25 source files reported, up from 24). Decided scripts/audit-git-identities.ts is out of scope for 100/100/100: its uncovered branches are defensive error paths in streamGit (timeout, spawn failure, stdin error) that cannot be triggered without mocking, plus the untestable entry-point guard.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Nine review rounds on PR 10. Four consecutive Majors in the write path, each a genuine escalation of the previous fix rather than a repeat: bundle self-containment (a header-vs-payload comparison did not close it, because removing an object from both leaves them consistent and wrong together — fixed by importing into an isolated object store and walking full ancestry, plus asserting blob presence because flattenTree never reads blob content); then lexical path traversal; then symbolic links, which bypass any lexical rule because git tracks links and writeFileSync follows them; then an arbitrary repository-INTERNAL target, where bundle .git/config passed every guard and would have overwritten the maintainer's git configuration with bundle bytes on self-host:write. The last was fixed structurally rather than by blacklisting names: the target must already be tracked by git or not exist at all, because what the bundle IS is tracked source, and an existing untracked file is never a legitimate target. Also fixed in these rounds: a history-loss path where a bundle not advertising the ref silently restarted history and the verifier could not detect it because it compares tip trees only; two verification inputs read from the dirty working tree the gate advertised it ignored; ls-files output being trimmed so a path with leading whitespace was compared against the wrong file; and a 658 MB per-run temp leak introduced by the fix for the coverage flakiness. The durable lesson is that these fixes were reactive rather than derived from a threat model of what a pull request can make --write do, since self-host.json arrives with the source.

patch.value: Phase 4 is delivered and merged in PR 10. pm-vcs now versions its own source in a bundle it wrote itself, and CI refuses a bundle whose tip tree is not byte-identical to the committed source. Every verification input is read from an extraction of HEAD rather than the working tree, so a dirty checkout cannot decide what the gate compares.
